key_insight: Tuna-2 shows that simple pixel (patch) embeddings — trained end-to-end from raw pixels — can replace pretrained vision encoders and provide a single unified visual representation that outperforms separate encoders for both understanding and generation.
problem_solved: Current unified multimodal models use pretrained vision encoders and separate visual representations for understanding vs. generation, causing task misalignment and preventing fully end-to-end optimization from raw pixels.
method: Replace pretrained vision backbones with lightweight patch/pixel embedding layers that convert raw pixels into token embeddings.
Use a single unified representation for both visual understanding and visual generation, enabling shared optimization and eliminating dual visual pipelines.
Train the full model end-to-end from pixels, aligning understanding and generation objectives within one architecture.
impact: Simpler architectures and end-to-end pixel training reduce modality misalignment and engineering complexity, enabling practitioners to build more efficient and better-aligned multimodal models for tasks like VQA, captioning, and image-conditioned generation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram comparing (a) traditional two-stream approach with pretrained vision encoder + separate generation tokens vs (b) Tuna-2 single pixel-embedding pipeline.

paper_title: Tuna-2: Pixel Embeddings Beat Vision Encoders for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
paper_authors: Zhiheng Liu, Weiming Ren, Xiaoke Huang, Shoufa Chen, Tianhong Li
